# How to Use Claude Code the Best

*Sources: 5 guides | Audience: Beginner*

## What You Should Know About Using Claude Code

Claude Code is an AI-powered assistant that lives in your terminal and can read, write, and reason about your entire codebase. If you're brand new to it, think of it less like a chatbot and more like a very capable junior developer that works inside your computer — you tell it what to build, it does the work, and you review the result.

Here's what matters most as a beginner:

### 1. Set Up Your Project Memory First

The very first thing you should do in any project is run `/init`. This creates a `CLAUDE.md` file — a plain text file that tells Claude Code everything it needs to know about your project: your coding style, folder structure, what tools you use. Once this file exists, Claude remembers your preferences every single session without you having to re-explain.

Think of `CLAUDE.md` as Claude's instruction manual for your project. The better it is, the less you have to repeat yourself.

### 2. One Task Per Chat Session

This is the single most important habit to build. When you finish a task, type `/clear` to start a fresh conversation. Don't let one session bleed into the next. Why? Claude has a "context window" — a limit to how much it can hold in memory at once. When that fills up, it starts forgetting earlier parts of your conversation, which causes mistakes.

**The rule:** one feature, one bug fix, one task per chat. `/clear` when done.

### 3. Plan Before You Code

Before asking Claude to write any code, use **Plan Mode** (press `Shift+Tab`). In plan mode, Claude will ask you clarifying questions and sketch out its approach before touching any files. This takes 2 extra minutes and saves you from having to undo 20 minutes of wrong work.

For anything bigger than a simple change, always plan first.

### 4. Give Claude Good Context

Claude Code is only as good as the context you give it. A vague prompt gets a vague result. Instead of "fix the login bug," say "the login form at `src/components/Login.tsx` is not validating the email field — fix the validation logic."

Use the `@` symbol to attach specific files to your message:
- `@./src/components/Login.tsx` — attach one file
- `@./src/api/` — attach a whole folder

The more specific you are, the better the result.

### 5. Manage Permissions Once, Not Every Time

Claude Code will ask for permission before doing things like editing files or running commands. You can approve these one by one, but a better approach for personal projects is to pre-configure your permissions in `.claude/settings.local.json` so Claude can work without stopping to ask every few minutes.

For beginners: start with approving things one at a time so you understand what Claude is doing. Once you trust it, open up the permissions.

### 6. Use Slash Commands to Save Your Workflows

Slash commands (like `/init`, `/clear`, `/compact`) are shortcuts for common actions. You can also **create your own** by adding a Markdown file to `.claude/commands/`. If you write a prompt you use over and over, turn it into a slash command.

### 7. When Things Go Wrong, Rewind — Don't Fix

If Claude does something you didn't want, don't try to correct it with more prompts. Use `/rewind` to go back to before it made the mistake, then try again with a clearer instruction. This is almost always faster than trying to patch over a wrong result.

### 8. Track Token Usage

Claude Code costs money based on how many tokens (roughly: words) you use. A few habits that keep costs down:
- `/clear` often — old context costs tokens even if it's not useful
- Use `/compact` to compress long conversations without losing the important parts
- For fast, cheap back-and-forth, toggle `/fast` mode

## Source Summaries

### Source 1: How I Use Claude Code (+ My Best Tips)
**Link:** [builder.io/blog/claude-code](https://www.builder.io/blog/claude-code)

**Key Points:**
- The author flipped their workflow: Claude Code is now the *primary* interface, with code review as secondary
- Pre-approve permissions upfront to avoid constant interruptions during a session
- Use `/clear` regularly to avoid unnecessary token compaction
- Keep Cursor or another IDE for quick tab completions; use Claude Code for substantive agent-based work
- The up arrow key retrieves previous chat history across sessions

**Most Important Takeaway:** Treat Claude Code as your main driver, not a helper. The mindset shift from "AI assistant" to "primary interface" is what unlocks its real value.

---

### Source 2: Claude Code CLI Cheatsheet
**Link:** [shipyard.build/blog/claude-code-cheat-sheet](https://shipyard.build/blog/claude-code-cheat-sheet/)

**Key Points:**
- Install with `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` (requires Node.js 18+)
- Use `-p "query"` flag to run Claude once and exit — great for scripts
- Use `-c` flag to continue your most recent conversation
- Configure granular permissions — don't just allow everything; restrict sensitive ops like `.env` reads
- Use hooks to auto-format code after Claude writes files (e.g., auto-run Black on Python files)
- Toggle extended thinking with `Option+T` (Mac) / `Alt+T` (Windows) for hard problems

**Most Important Takeaway:** The `@` syntax and hierarchical `CLAUDE.md` files are your biggest time-savers. Learn both early.

---

### Source 3: How to Use Claude Code — Slash Commands, Agents, Skills, and Plug-ins
**Link:** [producttalk.org/how-to-use-claude-code-features](https://www.producttalk.org/how-to-use-claude-code-features/)

**Key Points:**
- Layered `CLAUDE.md` files: global (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`) → project → subfolder. More specific files override general ones
- Only give Claude the context it needs for the current task — don't dump everything in
- Sub-agents work in separate context windows, keeping your main window clean
- Skills are bundles of prompts + context you can share across machines or with teammates
- Hooks guarantee certain things always happen, regardless of what Claude "decides"
- Access the official plugin marketplace with `/plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official`

**Most Important Takeaway:** Don't try to use every feature at once. Pick one building block (slash commands, or agents, or hooks) and go deep before adding more.

---

### Source 4: Claude Code Tutorial — Build a YouTube Research Agent Using Slash Commands
**Link:** [creatoreconomy.so/p/claude-code-tutorial-build-a-youtube-research-agent-in-15-min](https://creatoreconomy.so/p/claude-code-tutorial-build-a-youtube-research-agent-in-15-min)

**Key Points:**
- Start in **Plan Mode** (`Shift+Tab`) before writing any code to avoid wasted effort
- Set up `.claude/settings.local.json` with allowed tools so Claude can work autonomously
- Slash commands can accept parameters — you can build reusable, dynamic workflows
- Multi-step development: write specs → convert to to-do list → build → test → scale
- Claude Code is not just for coding — it's an "everything agent" for research, analysis, and automation

**Most Important Takeaway:** Giving Claude a clear specification document before it starts is the single biggest quality improvement you can make.

---

### Source 5: Cooking with Claude Code — The Complete Guide
**Link:** [sidbharath.com/blog/claude-code-the-complete-guide](https://sidbharath.com/blog/claude-code-the-complete-guide/)

**Key Points:**
- Always create a new git branch before starting a feature — never work on main
- Use `/rewind` instead of trying to fix a mistake with more prompts
- Git worktrees let you run multiple Claude instances in parallel on different features
- Use `/compact [instructions]` to compress context while preserving the parts that matter
- MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers let Claude access external tools without filling the context window
- The `&` prefix sends long tasks to Claude Code Web so you can keep working locally

**Most Important Takeaway:** Safety first: branch, rewind, and `/compact` are the three habits that prevent the most painful mistakes.
